citations.title: Healthcare Quality Workforce: A Sector in Demand (2024 Workforce Report)
citations.what_it_says: Documents CPHQ as the field's standard credential, with certified professionals commanding meaningfully higher salaries and broader role mobility across hospitals, payers, and consulting.

citations.title: Healthcare Quality Competency Framework and the CPHQ Examination
citations.what_it_says: Describes the eight-domain competency framework underpinning CPHQ and validates the credential's alignment with quality, safety, and PI job functions.

citations.title: Validation of the Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality Examination
citations.what_it_says: Provides psychometric validation of the CPHQ and links credential attainment with role advancement in hospital quality and patient-safety departments.

citations.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Medical and Health Services Managers
citations.what_it_says: Projects 28% growth 2022-2032 for health services managers (including quality/PI directors), the role family where CPHQ is most frequently listed as preferred.

citations.authors: Singer SJ, Rivard PE, Hayes JE, et al.
citations.title: Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Workforce Capacity in U.S. Hospitals
citations.what_it_says: Identifies persistent shortages of formally trained quality/safety personnel in U.S. hospitals, supporting sustained demand for CPHQ-credentialed staff.

citations.title: Competencies for Healthcare Quality Professionals: A Cross-Sectional Analysis
citations.what_it_says: Maps CPHQ exam domains to employer-stated competencies, finding strong alignment with hospital and payer quality roles but limited overlap with EHR-vendor technical roles.

citations.title: CPHQ Certification Handbook
citations.what_it_says: Specifies the $499 member exam fee, absence of formal eligibility prerequisites, and recommended experience, defining the credential's accessibility profile.
